title: Backend Engineer
mission: Build and maintain the booking, scheduling and invoicing system that Northlight's crews and customers use every day.
outcomes_90_days: Read the existing code and fix the most painful open bugs in the first month
Make double booking of a crew member impossible in the data layer, not only in the screen
Add tests around booking, invoicing and payment handling before changing them
Set up simple monitoring so the team knows about a failure before a customer does
Ship one customer visible improvement agreed with the office team

criteria.name: Backend development
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Has built and owned server side code in a mainstream language and framework, including real features used by real people.
evidence_needed: A named language and framework with what they built
Features shipped and who used them
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows the person building and owning server side code in production, with real examples

criteria.name: Database design
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Designs tables and constraints that fit the data, writes sound queries and changes a live schema safely.
evidence_needed: A schema they designed or changed
Migrations, indexes or constraints used for a reason
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows database design and safe schema changes with real examples

criteria.name: APIs and integrations
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Has designed or consumed web APIs and connected outside services such as payments, text messages or calendars.
evidence_needed: An integration they built and what went wrong or right
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows building web APIs or integrating outside services, with real examples

criteria.name: Testing and quality
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Writes automated tests, takes part in code review and keeps changes small and safe.
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows automated testing and review habits with real examples

criteria.name: Deployment and operations
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Can ship to a live server, roll back, and watch logs and uptime without a large team.
evidence_needed: Monitoring or logging they set up
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows deploying and running a service, including monitoring and rollback

criteria.name: Production debugging
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Finds the root cause of a live problem with logs and data, fixes it and prevents a repeat.
evidence_needed: A specific incident and the cause
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows tracking down and fixing a live problem to its root cause

criteria.name: Working with non technical people
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Turns office and crew needs into clear requirements and explains trade offs in plain words.
evidence_needed: A time they explained a trade off
Demos or documentation for non technical users
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows explaining technical choices to non technical colleagues, with real examples

gates.question: Can the person legally work in the country of the role?

work_sample.title: No double booking
work_sample.brief: Describe in a page, with a small table design and a few lines of code or pseudocode, how you would make sure one technician can never be booked for two overlapping jobs, even if two office staff click at the same moment.
work_sample.how_to_score: Score for a data level guarantee (constraint or transaction), handling of the failure case and clear writing. Do not score code style or the language chosen.

interview_questions.question: Walk me through the most important feature you built that real people used. What would you change now?
good_answer_signs: Honest list of what they would change

interview_questions.question: How would you add a new required column to a table with live data and no downtime?
good_answer_signs: Adds nullable first, backfills, then enforces
weak_answer_signs: Runs one big change on the live table

interview_questions.question: Tell me about a live bug that was hard to find. What did you look at first?
good_answer_signs: A fix plus a guard against a repeat

interview_questions.question: A payment provider sends the same webhook twice. What happens in your system?
good_answer_signs: Uses an idempotency key or stored event id
Logs and alerts on odd events

red_flags: Long technology lists with no sentence about what was built
Cannot name a bug they personally fixed
Claims a senior title but describes only small edits
sourcing_channels: Local and remote job boards the owner uses
Referrals from other small business owners
Open source and portfolio search through public web search
Bootcamp and community college alumni groups
pay_research_hint: Look at published pay ranges for backend and web developer roles in your region and at similar company sizes. Ask a technical advisor or a local developer group what a fair range looks like.
automation_note: An AI coding assistant can speed up routine code and tests. Someone still has to own the system, decide trade offs and answer when a live problem hits.
